title: run.sh runs the whole pipeline, including extraction (run-scripts slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of `docs/plans/run-scripts.md`, implementing the design landed in **#203**.

`./scripts/run.sh` now runs the whole pipeline: `index → fetch → select → estimate → extract`, each skipping what is already done. Cached transcripts are not refetched; batches already in the claim store are not re-extracted.

### The two arguments, which are not the same thing

- **`--batch 3`** names ONE batch and **refuses** if it is already stored. Naming a batch that is done is a mistake worth reporting.
- **`--batches 3`** says how many **pending** batches to work through, and **skips** stored ones without comment. Skipping what is done is the whole point of asking for a count.

Giving both is an **error**, not a precedence rule — a precedence rule is a thing readers guess at.

**Neither means `--batches 1`.** One, because that is the state the owner starts in: the numbers are unfamiliar until the calibration batch reports. Defaulting to `all` would make the first run the largest one, which is the opposite of what the calibration batch exists for.

### Two exit-code decisions that carry the design's meaning

**A ceiling stop ends the LOOP, not just the batch.** A run that has reached R26's line must not start another batch to discover the same thing again. It names what landed, what remains, and what the meter read, and exits non-zero.

**Completing the requested count exits 0, even with batches still pending.** Stopping because you asked for one batch is not a failure, and an exit code saying otherwise would make a normal continuation read as a recovery.

### `run.sh`

Arguments split at the first token that is not a stage name, so `./scripts/run.sh extract --batches all` works **without the wrapper knowing what `--batches` means**. Stages own their flags (R1006); a wrapper that parsed them would be a second place to keep in step. Arguments with more than one stage named are an error, because a flag one stage declared is not a flag the others did.

Its header claimed *"Nothing in this script spends money."* It will. The header now says what bounds it instead: the projection printed first, one batch by default, and R26's ceiling read from the real meter.

### Blind test authorship

`Blind-Tests: run-scripts-2`. **49 cases**, proved under **15 mutations**, each caught by the right tests: default-to-all, `--batch` as an alias for `--batches`, both arguments allowed, `--batches` refusing a stored batch, the ceiling stopping only the current batch, non-zero after a completed count, zero after a ceiling stop, `pending_batches` ignoring the store, ignoring which bundles exist, taking the last pending batch instead of the first, never saying what remains, `run.sh` not forwarding flags, `extract` missing from the default stages, the stale no-spend header kept, and the validator rejecting `extract`.

**No test executes `run.sh`** — it would invoke a model and spend real money — so its tests read the script's text. An autouse fixture fails any test that starts a process at all, so a seam guessed wrong cannot quietly become a real spend.

**One mutation exposed a defect in the tests themselves, and the author said so:** the meter's label `Weekly (7-day)` made a "batch 7 is still pending" assertion pass vacuously on every run. Its report helper now strips that label, and every fake number is built from digits that cannot impersonate a batch id.

**1853 passing, no disagreement between the two halves at assembly.**

### Ambiguities the author named rather than guessed

- **`--batches N` beyond the pending count** yields what remains rather than erroring. Not ruled by the plan; one test names the choice.
- **`pending_batches` is ascending** — the only order consistent with "calibration batch first", but the plan does not say it.
- **`--batches banana` or `--batches 0`** is refused by the parser here; the author asserted nothing, since several behaviours are defensible.
- **Whether a set-aside bundle should stop the loop** is unruled. Only the ceiling case is specified, and only that is implemented.

### Verified locally

1853 passing (49 new). `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean. `mypy src tests` clean over 58 files. `bash -n scripts/run.sh` clean, and the four argument shapes checked by hand. `plan-resolve.sh` resolves `run-scripts`. `blind-tests.sh` reports every blind-written test unmodified since its authoring commit.
